i.norm: Verifies that {@link PercentCodec} honors a custom set of "always encode" characters and that encoding followed by decoding returns the original input (a round-trip).

The input mixes: - lower-case letters a, b, c that are configured to always be percent-encoded - characters 1,2,3,_,-,.,* that must be left untouched - the Greek letters alpha (U+03B1) and beta (U+03B2), which are non US-ASCII and so are always percent-encoded as their UTF-8 byte sequences.
Configure the codec so that the bytes for 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f' are always encoded, and spaces are NOT turned into '+'.
Encode the input and read the result back as text for an easy-to-read comparison.
a/b/c -> %61/%62/%63, the safe characters pass through, alpha -> %CE%B1, beta -> %CE%B2.
Decoding the encoded bytes must reproduce the original input exactly.
